report.summary: The only failure is tests.api.test_book_can_be_updated, and it is a test bug: the test sends year=2001 but asserts the stored year is 2002. The app stores and returns the value it was given, so the fix is to correct the expected value in the test (line 27) to 2001, not to change the application.

causes.title: Update test expects year 2002 after sending 2001
causes.explanation: test_book_can_be_updated PUTs year=2001 and then asserts the GET returns year=2002. The update handler writes book.year unchanged into the database and returns it, so the correct value is 2001. The failing assertion compares against a hard-coded value that does not match the input. Nothing in the app adds one to the year.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:215-218: UPDATE books SET title = ?, author = ?, year = ? ... with book.year, then returns {"id": book_id, **book.model_dump()}
Failure detail: 'Differing items: {'year': 2001} != {'year': 2002}', so the response has the sent year and the test expectation is the odd one out.
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 27, change "year": 2002 to "year": 2001 (or reuse a variable for the 2001 literal so the two cannot drift apart). Then rerun the test.
